records.name: Arorha
records.held_by: Arorha village elders, answering to the Aroxhu council
records.summary: Arorha is a clay-mound village on the southern shore of Hatandros Bight, the confederacy's sea door. Its people ship Okuwun-Rahei clay and dye north to Thorn and south to Archon, and take tolls from boats that land.

notes.text: Arorha is the north-eastern outlier of the Aroxhu clay-mound country, a village on the first raised ground south of Hatandros Bight where the road from Inoja meets the sea. It exists to move the confederacy's clay, dye and pottery onto coastal boats. UESP has no page for it.

The mounds were raised by the village's founders, a generation or two after the Knahaten Flu emptied the coast of Cantemiric Velothi, over ground the Velothi had left fallow. In the Third Era the East Empire Company's boats called here for clay; in 4E 201 the landing is the same and the buyers are Argonian.

A working village with a short stone-free quay of piled mud-brick and wattle where flat boats unload. Elders from Arorha sit on the Aroxhu council. The warden post at Marshgate Watch to the north takes a toll on goods bound for Thorn, and Arorha pays it grudgingly.

About eleven Argonians of the Oxhu-Teeleel, mostly clay-diggers, potters and boatmen. The elder is a pot-painter who keeps the village's tally of kilns and boats. Two or three Dunmer traders from Thorn lodge here in the dry months.

Red clay, ochre and fired pots go out by boat; salt, dried fish and Thorn's saltrice come back. The tolls Arorha charges outsiders landing on its quay pay for the mound walls. Unfired clay is cheap here, finished glazed ware costs three times as much at Thorn.
The village keeps a hatching-tree at Aroxhu, three days' walk inland, and sends its eggs there. A small clay shrine on the quay holds votive pots to the dead; broken ones are left for the tide.

A ring of low red mounds, each carrying two or three reed-thatched houses on stilts, stained rust-brown by the clay. Kilns smoke at the water's edge and the shore is crazed red mud. Gulls and swamp-herons crowd the quay at dawn.
Inside the village it is calm. On the shore road to the north, mudcrab swarms and fleshflies are the daily trouble, and outlaws from Skeith Isle sometimes land in the dark to take boats.

The elder wants a lost kiln-load of ochre found: the boat that carried it was taken by Skeith smugglers. A broken Velothi ancestor-tablet from Virtluush has turned up in the clay-pits and an old Dunmer trader will pay to know where it came from.

records.name: Bala Karag
records.held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts and sea-birds
records.summary: Bala Karag is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi stronghold on a small rocky peninsula a day's walk from Thorn. The Knahaten Flu emptied it and the sea has taken its lower halls.

notes.text: A ruined Velothi hold on the rock off the Thorn coast, the nearest of the Hatandros Bight ruins to the city. It has no UESP page; its name is the map's, and its Velothi character follows from the Cantemiric Velothi's canon range between Archon, Arnesia and Thorn.

Cantemiric Velothi, Dunmer dissidents who settled the eastern seaboard, held this coast until the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 killed them all. Nobody has lived here since. Chimeri myth says Mephala led a third of the Velothi into Black Marsh.

Empty except for the dead. Thorn's slavers and, later, the Warden Marches' toll men both left it alone, and the Argonians of the coast call it sick ground. The tide floods the lowest hall twice a day.
No living inhabitants. Ancestor ghosts of the Velothi walk the halls, for the Velothi buried their dead beneath their houses and the flu killed whole families at once.
Once a fortified holding that taxed coastal boats. Now it draws scavengers: Velothi bronze, ash-glass and carved ancestor tablets sell at Thorn to Dunmer buyers.

The Velothi who came south followed the Mephala-led exile and kept ancestor veneration. Tablets and altar niches remain in the upper halls; the Argonians who pass by say the place is sick and do not leave offerings.

Grey basalt and black volcanic stone in heavy, battered Velothi courses, half drowned at the base and crusted with barnacles and salt. A broken tower stands on the rock with a causeway that only shows at low tide.
Ghosts and skeletons in the halls, cliff-nesting hackwings outside, and a tide that can trap anyone who goes in on the ebb and stays past it.
A Dunmer relic-seller in Thorn will pay for a particular ancestor tablet carved with the family sign of the holding's last lord. The lowest hall has a sealed door only the ghosts can open.

terrain_needs.why: the ruin stands on its rocky peninsula
the hall entrance is cut into the rock

records.name: Kornakim
records.held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts
records.summary: Kornakim is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi watch-hold on a sandy headland halfway down Hatandros Bight. It was abandoned after the Knahaten Flu and sits above the surf, shunned.

notes.text: A ruined Velothi coastal hold on the headland at the bight's seaward edge. UESP has no page for Kornakim; the map names it and the Cantemiric Velothi are canon for this coast.

Cantemiric Velothi built along the eastern seaboard between Archon and Thorn and died in the Knahaten Flu (2E 560). Kornakim's position on a seaward point suggests a watch-hold over the sea lanes, which is our reading, not canon.
Roofless but standing. A smuggler's lantern sometimes burns on the headland, though the smugglers do not go inside.
Nobody lives here. The ruin is known to the Skeith smugglers as a landmark and to the Arorha clay-men as a place not to dig.
Once a watch-hold that signalled the Velothi's boats. Now a landmark for blockade-runners and a source of ash-glass shards that wash up on the beach below.
Velothi ancestor shrine niches line the inner hall. The ghosts of the hold's household remain at their posts.
Dark Velothi stonework in low rounded courses with a broken watch-tower at the seaward end, sand drifting into the courtyard, sea-grass growing through the floor, surf loud against the headland.
Ancestor ghosts within, crabs and hackwings on the beach, and a sinkhole in the courtyard that goes down to the sea cave beneath.

A signal brazier at the top of the tower still holds a spell-lit fire that no one has put out. A smuggler's cache is hidden in the sea cave beneath the hall, left behind by a crew that did not come back.

terrain_needs.why: stands on the headland above the beach
hall entrance in the headland's landward slope

records.name: Coldbrine Mine
records.held_by: Warden Marches families of Thorn, under Fort Thornmoth
records.summary: Coldbrine Mine is a rock-salt working in a low bluff south-west of Thorn, held by the Warden Marches. Its salt cures the saltrice and fish that Thorn exports.

notes.text: A small rock-salt mine in the rise between Thorn and the bight, worked by Thorn's field-owners' hired hands. The name is ours, in the Warden Marches' plain Imperial naming style; it has no UESP page.
Imperial-era bonded labour first cut the salt-bed for the East Empire Company's saltrice and fish trade; the shafts were kept running by Thorn's field-owners after the Company left.
A handful of workers cut brine-hard salt blocks in two shafts and load them on carts. A warden from Fort Thornmoth checks the tally each month and takes a levy.
About five Argonians, descendants of freed labourers, plus a warden-appointed overseer from an old Archein family who keeps the ledger and the keys.
Rock-salt for curing: blocks go to Thorn, ground salt to Arorha for fish. The salt is cheap but its trade is steady.
The workers carry small hatching-stones from their home villages and leave a pinch of salt at the mine mouth for those buried underground.
A cut face of grey-white rock streaked with rust, a timber headframe, wooden carts and stacked salt blocks under reed roofs. The air smells of brine and wet stone.
Cave-ins in the older shaft, brine pools with rotting water, and mudcrabs that nest in the spoil heap.

The old shaft was sealed after a collapse that killed bonded labourers; one of their descendants wants the bodies recovered and the overseer refuses. Something has been cutting a new gallery at night.

terrain_needs.why: the mine mouth is cut into a bluff

records.name: Marshgate Watch
records.held_by: Archwardens, detachment from Fort Thornmoth
records.summary: Marshgate Watch is a road post on the coast road south of Thorn. Wardens check goods and travellers moving between Thorn, the bight villages and Arorha.

notes.text: A small garrison post where the Thorn road crosses the neck of land at the bight's northern end. The name is ours, in the Marches' naming habit; no UESP page exists.

Built by the Imperial Commission as a toll and way-station for the Thorn-Archon road, abandoned in the Interregnum, and reoccupied by the Archwardens' detachment when the frontier screen needed a customs point on the east road.
Six wardens rotate through from Fort Thornmoth. They stamp cargo bills, take a levy on clay and salt, and watch the shore for boats that avoid Thorn.
Six Argonian wardens of old Archein lines, in patched half-Imperial livery, led by a sergeant who keeps the paper and the post's one cutlass.
Tolls, on a scale of a few septims per cart. The post buys fish and bread from Arorha and sells nothing.
None officially. The wardens go home to their village trees to hatch and bury, and have little faith in the post.
A square stone-and-timber blockhouse on a mud-brick plinth, a toll bar across the road, a signal pole, and a few huts of reed round it.
Fleshflies, swamp-crocodiles in the ditch, and smugglers landing by night who will fight rather than pay.
A customs bill for a cargo that never arrived is on the sergeant's desk. A warden has been taking bribes from Skeith smugglers, and the sergeant wants it proven.

records.name: Wreck of the Pale Harvest
records.held_by: No one; sea creatures and the drowned crew
records.summary: The Pale Harvest was an East Empire Company saltrice freighter that went down in Hatandros Bight. Its cargo of rotted sacks and a ship's strongbox are still aboard.

notes.text: A sunken saltrice freighter on the seabed of the bight, a short swim from the shore near Ysan. The ship and its name are AGENT_INVENTED; no UESP page exists for a wreck here.

sources.title: Saltrice is the East Empire Company export at Thorn (argonia-4e201-state.md)

notes.text: One of the Company's last saltrice runs from Thorn to Archon before the province closed, sunk in a squall with the harvest aboard.

sources.title: Saltrice is the East Empire Company export at Thorn (argonia-4e201-state.md)

notes.text: Barnacled and half-buried in silt. The hull is intact enough to enter; the cargo has long since turned to black sludge.

sources.title: Saltrice is the East Empire Company export at Thorn (argonia-4e201-state.md)

notes.text: Nobody. The drowned crew remain aboard as drowned dead.

sources.title: Saltrice is the East Empire Company export at Thorn (argonia-4e201-state.md)

notes.text: A strongbox of Company coin and ship's papers is the draw. Salvagers from Ysan and Arorha have picked at the hull but not reached the hold.

notes.text: A listing timber hull on grey silt, barnacled ribs, rotten sacks heaped in the hold, ropes drifting in the green light.

sources.title: Saltrice is the East Empire Company export at Thorn (argonia-4e201-state.md)

records.name: Zeeraxun Roost
records.held_by: The Sarpa of the Zeeraxun roost
records.summary: Zeeraxun Roost is a camp of the winged Sarpa on a rise in the marsh behind Hatandros Bight. They keep apart and drive off outsiders, and stay near the Virtluush ruin.

notes.text: A permanent camp of Sarpa, one of the winged interior breeds, on high ground behind the bight. The name is ours; canon gives the Sarpa no camps here. No UESP page.
Sarpa are canon as exclusive to Middle Argonia; a camp on the eastern edge is an extension of their range, sited here because the Virtluush ruin offers high stone to roost on.
A camp of tents and perches, with scouts on the wing at dawn. The Sarpa watch the road to Arorha and shoo off clay-diggers who come near.
About nine Sarpa, led by an old female who speaks Jel and a few words of Dunmeri. They are cautiously willing to trade for dye and salt if a visitor approaches openly.
Feathers, bird-eggs and fish; they trade for salt and clay beads at the edge of their ground. Ash-glass picked from Virtluush is their one valuable good.
The Sarpa hold the wind to be a messenger of the Hist and read omens in flight patterns. They keep a rack of old Velothi ancestor-bones on a post as a boundary mark.
Tents of woven reed and hide on a rise, tall poles with feathered streamers, nets slung between trees, droppings white on the stones.
Sarpa archers attack intruders at range from the air; the camp's boundary poles are marked in feathers and bones.
The Sarpa want a stolen Velothi bone-flute back from an Arorha potter. The old female will trade safe passage across the Virtluush ground for it.

records.name: Virtluush
records.held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts and Sarpa scouts
records.summary: Virtluush is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi settlement inland of Hatandros Bight, once a river-fort. A Sarpa roost sits beside it.

notes.text: A bigger Velothi ruin on a river bend behind the bight, with a Sarpa camp at its flank. It has no UESP page; the Velothi are canon for this seaboard.
A Cantemiric Velothi holding, ended by the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560. The river gave it a boat road to the coast, which is our reading of its siting.
Collapsed courts, a standing tower, and a deep cistern, haunted. The Sarpa live beside it and take ash-glass and tablets from the edges but will not go into the lower halls.
No living folk inside. Velothi ancestor ghosts in the lower halls and a lich-like household warden are an AGENT_INVENTED guard.
Once a river-fort that taxed boat traffic. Now a scavenger's draw: Velothi bronze, ash-glass, ancestor tablets and a vault of stored dye-stuffs.
Mephala-influenced Velothi ancestor worship: altar niches to a Daedric lord and carved family tablets in every room.
Black stone courts and a tall broken tower in heavy Velothi courses, ivy and vines over the walls, a cistern with dark water in the heart.
Ancestor ghosts, skeletal guards, and a Sarpa lookout who will shoot anyone who approaches by air or reed-path.
A house-lord's ghost still holds a ring of the family seal; the Dunmer relic-seller in Thorn will pay for the ring. The cistern is connected to the bight by a drowned tunnel.

terrain_needs.why: the ruin stands on the river bend's bank
hall entrance cut into the bank

records.name: Ysan
records.held_by: Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac, a landing held for Tsonac
records.summary: Ysan is a small coastal landing of Tsonac's stone-building people on Hatandros Bight. Quarried stone and timber come down here by river to be shipped to Thorn.

notes.text: A hamlet at the bight's northern shore where the Tsonac-Kaleel's stone and timber reach the sea. It has no UESP page; its culture is Tsonac's by the map.
Founded as a coast landing by Tsonac when Thorn's stone-hunger returned after the Great War; the freight path down from the jungle uplands is older than the hamlet.
A busy river-mouth landing with a stone jetty, a lime kiln and loading sheds. Thorn boats call in the dry season.
About six Argonians of Tsonac who move between the uplands and the shore, with a Thorn broker who lodges here during the dry months.
Cut stone, hewn timber and lime go out to Thorn; salt, rope and cloth come in. Tsonac keeps the price of stone higher than Thorn would like.
They carry small tokens of Tsonac's sleeping Hist, a tree-minder's charm of resin to sleep by, and do not pray to it in public.
A neat dry-stone jetty, stacked blocks sorted by size, lime-white dust on the reeds, and a few terraced stilt-houses with stone footings on the shore.
Fleshflies and crocodiles in the river mouth; the Tsonac men watch for Thorn's slavers' successors, whom they despise.
A shipment of carved lintel stones for a Thorn client has gone missing between Tsonac and the jetty. The quarry-men suspect the smugglers on Skeith.

records.name: Yuva-Goli
records.held_by: Root-Folk of Helstrom, tide-station
records.summary: Yuva-Goli is a Root-Folk station on the outer coast of Hatandros Bight, the Hist forest's one watch on the Padomaic. Its few people gather tide-wrack and sea-salt and keep a lookout.

notes.text: A hamlet of Helstrom's people, set on the open coast far from any Hist tree. It has no UESP page; the Root-Folk's hunting and egg-tending stations spread through the inner swamp, and this is their sea outlier.
Founded when the Root-Folk wanted ears on the sea, after the Umbriel year; its people came from the Lake Ulaish country by canoe.
Five Root-Folk keep the station and rotate home after a season. They watch ships and trade quietly with Arorha.
About five Saxhleel. The eldest has the status of a mid-ranked tree-minder and speaks to Helstrom through a sap-jar sent twice a year.
Dried sea-salt, sea-kelp for dyeing, tide-wrack and eggs of sea-birds; they take in news and trade it for clay and pottery from Arorha.
Without a Hist near, they keep a sealed sap-jar from Helstrom on a shrine and read it as their counsel; they do not speak of the sea.
A cluster of reed-and-root stilt houses above the tide line, drying racks of kelp, canoes drawn up on mud, nets in a line.
Surf, crabs and hackwings on the shore; the station's folk do not like uninvited visitors and will report them to Helstrom.
The sap-jar has gone cloudy and the elder fears the Hist is ill. Someone has to carry a fresh jar from Helstrom, or find what is poisoning this one.

records.name: Wreck of the Silt Bride
records.held_by: No one; the drowned dead of the hold
records.summary: Wreck of the Silt Bride is A Dunmer slaver brig lost off the coast of Thorn in the late Third Era. Her hold still holds shackles and a ledger of captives.

notes.text: Wreck of the Silt Bride is a Dunmer slaver brig lost off the coast of Thorn in the late Third Era. Her hold still holds shackles and a ledger of captives. The ship and its name are AGENT_INVENTED; there is no UESP page for it.

sources.title: Lore:Wreck of the Silt Bride (searched 2026-11-08: no page)

notes.text: A Dres-chartered slaver of the kind that sailed from Thorn after the Arnesian War and into Helseth's ban, sunk in a storm with captives aboard. Slavers were still active in Arnesia in the latemost Third Era.
The brig lies on her side in the shelf off Thorn, hull split amidships, the stern cabin intact.
No one lives here. The slaver's crew drowned in the hold with their captives, and the shackled dead are the ones seen moving in the cabin at low tide.
Dunmer relic-collectors and ledger-hunters pay for the captain's logbook; Thorn's Archwardens would pay more to bury it.
Thorn's coast Argonians do not pray at the Silt Bride, for she carried their kin in chains. They leave a painted shell on the nearest shore for the captives, and spit on the water over the hull.
A black-oaked hull furred with weed, rusted shackles trailing from the hatch, fish in the cabin windows.
Drowned dead in the hold, slaughterfish, and a current that pulls toward the split in the hull. The depth is a short swim from shore.
The logbook names the Dunmer families who bought captives from Thorn; some of them still trade there. The Thorn Vicecanon wants it, as do the families it names.

terrain_needs.why: the wreck lies on the sea floor

records.name: Wreck of the Brindle Gull
records.held_by: No one; the drowned dead of the sloop
records.summary: Wreck of the Brindle Gull is A smuggler's sloop that foundered off Kornakim fleeing a warden cutter, with a hidden compartment still sealed.

notes.text: Wreck of the Brindle Gull is a smuggler's sloop that foundered off Kornakim fleeing a warden cutter, with a hidden compartment still sealed. The ship and its name are AGENT_INVENTED; there is no UESP page for it.

sources.title: Lore:Wreck of the Brindle Gull (searched 2026-11-08: no page)

notes.text: A fast sloop running untaxed goods from Skeith Isle to the Arorha shore; she ran onto the Kornakim shoals in a squall within the last twenty years.
The hull rests upright in shallow green water, mast broken at the step, the deckhouse hatch still shut.
No one lives here. The smuggler crew went down off the Kornakim shoals, and only the captain is said to stay, on guard over the strongbox.
Her cargo, moon-sugar casks gone to rot and a strongbox of Skeith coin, is the draw; Skeith crews dive for it and do not tell the wardens.
Skeith smugglers drop a coin in the water above the Brindle Gull before a night run, for luck against the wardens. Arorha's fishers leave a knotted cord on the shore for the crew.
A small clinker hull with a painted gull on the bow, soft with weed, with spars and lines floating above it.
Slaughterfish and a drowned dead captain who guards the strongbox; the water is shallow but the shoal bottom is jagged.
The sloop's logbook shows the route and a landing the wardens do not know about, and the Skeith smugglers would kill to keep it secret.

terrain_needs.why: the wreck lies on the sea floor

records.name: Wreck of the Resolute Crest
records.held_by: No one; the drowned marines
records.summary: Wreck of the Resolute Crest is A Septim Navy man-of-war of the Far East Fleet, sunk in deep water with its ballistae and an Akaviri chest still aboard.

notes.text: Wreck of the Resolute Crest is a Septim Navy man-of-war of the Far East Fleet, sunk in deep water with its ballistae and an Akaviri chest still aboard. The ship and its name are AGENT_INVENTED; there is no UESP page for it.

sources.title: Lore:Wreck of the Resolute Crest (searched 2026-11-08: no page)

notes.text: Uriel Septim V's Far East Fleet sailed the Padomaic against Akavir in the 3E 270s; this ship went down on the return run, long before the province left the Empire.
The great hull rests on the deep shelf east of Skeith Isle, upright, weedgrown, the quarterdeck still above the silt.
No one lives here. The marines of the Far East Fleet went down with the ship, and their drowned dead still stand watch on the quarterdeck.
A chest of Akaviri tribute and the ship's brass sell for a fortune to a collector at Archon. The depth is the barrier, since only the skilled diver gets this deep.
Divers who reach the Resolute Crest salute the ensign before touching the chest, an old Imperial custom the wreck keeps alive. Skeith's crews tie a knotted cord at their camp for the Navy dead.
A tall black-oaked hull ringed with weed, a bronze figurehead of a crest worn smooth, ballistae on a sunken deck, shoals of fish.
Deep water, cold currents, drowned Imperial marines, sea-drakes and the pressure itself; this is a dive for the well-prepared.
A dying marine's letter of command is in the captain's cabin, naming a stash on Skeith Isle. A collector at Archon wants the chest.

terrain_needs.why: the wreck lies on the sea floor

records.name: Hollow Tide Camp
records.held_by: Skeith smugglers, a hardened crew
records.summary: Hollow Tide Camp is the smugglers' beach camp on the south-west of Skeith Isle. It runs untaxed goods between the isle and the Okuwun-Rahei shore, avoiding Archon and Thorn customs.

notes.text: A smuggler camp in the lee of Skeith Isle's low south-western bluffs. The name is ours; the map labels it only [Smuggler Camp]. No UESP page.

Argonia has three legal entries and a long coast; any unwatched beach near a customs port draws smugglers. Skeith's position between Thorn, Seafalls and Archon makes it the obvious cache for goods that avoid both customs houses.
About fourteen men and women live in lean-to huts above the tide line, with two hidden coves and a cache in the caves under the bluff. They bring in boats on the dark of the moons.

Mixed crews: Argonian boatmen of the Okuwun coast, a few Dunmer from Tear, runaway Archein families, Khajiit moon-sugar dealers. The leader is a former Archon harbour clerk who knows every customs rule.

They move moon sugar, salt, ash-glass, Dunmer wine and untaxed saltrice, and take a cut from every cargo. They are genuinely outlaw, unlike the chartered pirates of the north camp, and the two crews are rivals.
Mostly none; some Dunmer keep a Tribunal-era charm, some Argonians a village-tree token. Everyone shows the sea respect.
Lean-tos of driftwood, tarred canvas and reed roofs, boats hauled up on grey shingle, barrels hidden under nets, a smoking drying-rack.
Armed lookouts and a short fuse with strangers; the coves are trapped, and the bluff caves hold crocodiles the crew feed.
The leader will hire a stranger to carry a cargo past Marshgate Watch. A rival pirate crew has burned a boat, and war between the two camps is close.

records.name: Marque Landing
records.held_by: Skeith pirates, half-chartered ex-privateers
records.summary: Marque Landing is the pirates' camp on stilts in the shallows below Rainbreaker Keep. Its crews sail on a half-recognised letter of marque from the Archon coast tradition.

notes.text: A stilt-and-hulk pirate camp in the shallows on Skeith Isle's western shore, serving Rainbreaker Keep. The name is ours; the map labels it [Pirate Camp]. No UESP page exists.

The Archon coast was 'riddled with pirates' in the late First Era and General Lucinia Falco sent letters of marque to them; our reading is that the tradition survived as a half-chartered fleet in 4E 201, the state's substitute for a navy.
Four ships' crews share the camp. They hold the keep above as a strong room and raid shipping but leave Archon's own boats alone.
About twenty pirates, mostly Argonian boat-crews with a few Dunmer and Khajiit seamen. The pirate-captain, a one-eyed Argonian, has a letter that the Archwardens neither honour nor repudiate.
Prize cargoes, ransom, protection fees on coast boats, and the occasional state commission to chase a rival. They sell to Archon quietly.
A rough sea-faith: each ship has a carved figurehead they swear by, and the keep's dead are left to the tide.
A line of hulks and stilt-houses on grey water, ropes and nets slung between, a stone jetty at the keep's foot, smoke and lanterns.
Crossbow and fire-arrow lookouts and a camp that fights as a crew; the keep above is a stronghold, the water below is full of eels.
The captain wants a rival ship's chart taken from Hollow Tide Camp. A letter of marque, genuine or forged, would let the stranger sail as a chartered privateer.

records.name: The Grey Tooth
records.held_by: No one; sea-birds
records.summary: The Grey Tooth is the one crag on Skeith Isle, a grey-green stone spire that seamen use as a mark. The summit gives a view of the whole coast.

notes.text: A bare grey-green peak of dark, sea-worn rock at the island's centre, named by us for its look. It is not on UESP's list; the Arnesian island's dark green-grey terrain is canon.
Nothing is recorded of it. Seamen of every age have used it as a landmark, and the Imperial keep at the shore may have been built to watch it.
A seamark, with a rough cairn at the top and a goat-path up the south face. The pirates keep a lookout post on it in clear weather.
No residents. A lookout from Marque Landing climbs it in the day.
Nothing is made here. It serves as the lookout for both camps and the beacon-stone for boats on the Okuwun coast.
Sailors leave a pebble on the cairn for luck; the Argonians say the stone is a Hist's old bone, which is a story only.
A dark grey-green tooth of rock with sea-birds nesting in its cracks, thin salt-grass on the lower slopes, wind-bent shrubs.
Steep cliffs, loose rock and nesting hackwings, plus a pirate lookout who will shoot at strangers.
A smuggler's cache is hidden under the cairn; its map is on the wreck of the Stormwidow. A shaman's bones are said to lie in a cave on the north face.

records.name: Rainbreaker Keep
records.held_by: Marque Landing pirates, the Rainbreaker crew
records.summary: Rainbreaker Keep is an old Imperial sea-watch keep on Skeith Isle. The pirates of Marque Landing now use it as their strong room, and its undercroft has a dungeon.

notes.text: A stone keep on a rise by the shore of Skeith Isle, built by the Empire and now held by pirates. The name is the map's; there is no UESP page and its Imperial origin is read from its symbol and name.

Probably built in the late First Era when the Empire policed the Archon coast, to watch and break the pirate trade; the Third Empire kept it as a signal tower until the secession of 4E 6, when the garrison left.
Pirates took it in the last twenty years. They hold the upper hall as their moot-room and the lower vault as a strong room; the undercroft, once the garrison's cells, is the pirates' prison.
Twelve of the Marque Landing pirates live here under the quartermaster, with up to a dozen captives in the cells at a time.
A strong room for prize cargoes and ransom. Captives are kept for ransom or sold to buyers on the Okuwun coast.
An Imperial shrine to Akatosh in the chapel was left standing and is now stacked with crates; the pirates swear by their figureheads.
A squat square keep of grey stone with a signal tower, weather-pitted, a sea-wall and a stone jetty, hung with fishing nets and ships' lanterns.
Pirates, a locked strong room, trapped stairs, and flooded lower cells where the tide enters.
A captive in the cells knows where the Resolute Crest's chest lies. The quartermaster keeps a book of every prize and every bribe taken from wardens.

terrain_needs.why: keep on a rise above the shore

records.name: Wreck of the Stormwidow
records.held_by: No one; scavengers from both camps
records.summary: The Stormwidow is a privateer galleon driven onto the south-west beach of Skeith Isle. Both camps strip her, and her hold holds a stash the scavengers have not found.

notes.text: A beached ship on the south-west shore of Skeith Isle, partly above the tide line. The ship and her name are AGENT_INVENTED; no UESP page.

sources.title: Lore:Wreck of the Stormwidow (searched 2026-11-08: no page)

notes.text: A chartered privateer of the Archon coast, driven ashore in a gale and abandoned by her crew, who joined the Marque Landing camp.
Her upper hull is picked clean; the lower hold is full of sand and sea-water at high tide and rarely entered.
Nobody lives aboard. Scavengers from both camps sneak in at the ebb.
Timber, copper sheathing and cordage are stripped for the camps. The captain's strongbox is the real prize.
None; the pirates say the figurehead is bad luck and have turned it to face the sea.
A listing hull half-buried in grey sand, ribs open to the sky, ropes and sails rotting, a figurehead of a veiled woman.
Rotten decks, crabs in the hold and a rising tide; the camps will fight anyone they catch at the wreck.
The captain's strongbox holds a map to the cairn on the Grey Tooth. Both camps search for it and neither has found it.

records.name: Aroxhu
records.held_by: The council of village elders of the Oxhu-Teeleel, meeting under the Aroxhu Hist
records.summary: Aroxhu is the great mound-town of the Clay-Mound People, the largest tribal settlement of the east interior. Its council of elders speaks for the whole confederacy and meets under its Hist.

notes.text: The seat of the Oxhu-Teeleel confederacy, a mound-town of red clay with a Hist at its centre, 40-odd people at the map's small-city tier. UESP has no page for Aroxhu; the people, the confederacy and the council are ours, built on canon's many unnamed tribes.

Raised over generations on a clay ridge above the flood plain; it never held a stone wall. After the Umbriel year it took in the Arorha and Inoja families whose lowland villages were ruined, and became the confederacy's centre.
A busy mound-town: the council meets each new moon under the Hist, the potters' quarter fires day and night, and the Archwardens must bargain for any road or toll in Oxhu country.

About thirty-eight Argonians of the Oxhu-Teeleel: a council of seven elders (each from one village, with a speaker chosen yearly), potters, dyers, mound-farmers and boatmen, and a few visiting Agaceph traders.
Pottery, red clay, ochre and madder dye go down the rivers to Archon and Thorn; Aroxhu takes salt, fish, metal tools and coin. The clay trade is the confederacy's wealth and the Archwardens' envy.

The Aroxhu Hist is a young tree grown on the central mound. The elders hold the hatching rite beneath it, and eggs are laid in warm clay-pits at its roots. The town's dead go into the mounds beneath their houses.

A hill of terraced red mounds topped with a great gnarled Hist, reed-thatched houses on each terrace, kilns with long streamers of smoke, drying racks of cloth in madder red and ochre yellow, and a clay-paved moot-ground at the foot of the tree.
The town is safe; the elders keep a quiet watch of spear-bearers. The road to Inoja is a D1, but Sarpa and Paatru bands raid the outlying mounds.
A stolen clay-dye recipe has been sold to a Thorn guild and the council wants the thief found. Two villages dispute a mound boundary and the speaker needs a neutral go-between.

terrain_needs.why: the mounds rise above the plain

records.name: Inoja
records.held_by: Inoja elders, under the Aroxhu council
records.summary: Inoja is the market town of the clay-mound country, on the river crossing south of Aroxhu. It is the confederacy's main trading post for outsiders.

notes.text: A town of about twenty on the river fork where roads from Aroxhu, Arorha and the southern villages meet. It is where outsiders deal with the confederacy. No UESP page for Inoja exists.
Grew from a ferry crossing at a river fork into the confederacy's market, because Aroxhu does not want strangers inside its mounds and Inoja is a day's walk away.
A busy dry-season market. Dunmer clay-buyers from Thorn, Okuwun boatmen, and now and then a Khajiit trader bargain here. The elders rule disputes between buyers and sellers.
About twenty-one Argonians of the Oxhu-Teeleel: factors, boatmen, ferrymen and inn-keepers, with a handful of visiting Dunmer and Khajiit.
Clay, pottery and dye are sold in bulk; Inoja takes a market toll and runs the river ferry. Prices here are what Aroxhu allows.
Small clay shrines to the dead line the market; the Hist of Aroxhu is the town's tree, and its sap-gatherers walk there once a season.
Terraced mounds along the river, a broad market-ground with reed awnings and stacks of pots in red and brown, a rope ferry, and stilted inns over the water.
Safe in the town. Pickpockets, a few freelance Naga road-robbers on the river road, and floods that cut the crossing for days.
A buyer from Thorn has paid for a barge of pots that never arrived. The river ferryman saw something at night but will only tell a friend.

records.name: Joxhi
records.held_by: Joxhi elders, under the Aroxhu council
records.summary: Joxhi is a village of clay-diggers on a river bend north of Inoja. Its pits supply the finest red clay in the confederacy.

notes.text: A village beside a river bend in the northern mounds, known for its pits. No UESP page for Joxhi.
Its clay pit was found by a hatchling of the first Inoja families and has been dug for generations; the village is built on its own spoil.
A working village, wary of the tribal camps to the west and of Thorn's buyers who offer too much.
About ten Argonians of the Oxhu-Teeleel, mostly diggers and carriers; the elder is a former potter who still tests every cart.
Fine red clay dug in blocks and floated down the river to Inoja and Aroxhu. Joxhi clay fires to a deep brick-red that sells for double.
The village sends its eggs to Aroxhu. Diggers leave a clay figure in the pit for any lost to a collapse.
A village on stilted mounds beside a river bend, raw red pits edged by reed fencing, drying clay in blocks, an orange-stained river.
Pit collapses, crocodiles in the river mouth and Sarpa raiders from the west who come for tools.
A new seam of pale clay turned up in the pit that glows faintly at night; the elder wants to know what it is. An old Velothi tablet has come up in the spoil.

records.name: Gaweja
records.held_by: Gaweja elders, under the Aroxhu council
records.summary: Gaweja is a lakeside clay-mound village on the road between Yulca and Badal. It fishes, grows rice on its mound slopes and sells fish to the Agaceph.

notes.text: A village on the lake edge on the western side of the mound country, the border village with the Agaceph. No UESP page for Gaweja.
The clay-mound people's furthest settlement toward Yulca; founded as a fishing post, it became the place Oxhu and Agaceph meet to trade.
A quiet village; the elders keep a good relationship with Yulca, which is rare, and a fair at the lake's edge each autumn.
About eleven Argonians of the Oxhu-Teeleel, fishers and rice-growers, with a few Agaceph visitors.
Dried fish, eel-paste and rice go to Yulca and Aroxhu; Gaweja buys books and scrolls from the Agaceph, for the elder's sake.
Eggs go to Aroxhu. A fisher's shrine of woven reeds stands on the point with a cord for every boat lost.
Stilted mounds along the lake edge, drying racks of eel, rice terraces with water-lilies, reed boats pulled up, a small stone cairn on the point.
Lake crocodiles, leeches in the shallows and illusionist-tricked travellers from Yulca who come unfocused.
An Agaceph scholar has gone missing on the lake and Gaweja's fishers found his raft empty. Someone has been dredging the lake bed at night.

records.name: Renhu
records.held_by: Renhu elders, under the Aroxhu council
records.summary: Renhu is a coastal clay-mound village on an inlet east of Xibcan. Its people farm the mounds and net fish in the estuary.

notes.text: A village between the inlet and the road to Seafalls, with a view of Skeith Isle on clear days. No UESP page for Renhu.
A late daughter-village of Inoja, settled when the mounds filled; its position on the road makes it the stopping place for Seafalls-bound carts.
A tidy village with a small guesthouse and good fish. The elders watch for Skeith smugglers who sometimes buy their boats.
About twelve Argonians of the Oxhu-Teeleel, farmers and netters; a few Seafalls pilots lodge here.
Estuary fish, eels and rice; the guesthouse earns from travellers on the Seafalls road.
The village sends eggs inland to Aroxhu; the elder's family keeps a tide-chart carved on a clay tablet, which half the village thinks is a prayer.
Reed-thatched stilt houses on three low mounds by a muddy inlet, nets draped over poles, boats at a clay landing, gulls overhead.
Coastal crocodiles, fleshflies and nighttime smuggler landings on the inlet.
A boat sold to a stranger has turned up in Skeith's camp with the elder's name burned into the keel. A signal light has been seen on the bluff at night.

records.name: Khiar
records.held_by: Khiar elders, under the Aroxhu council
records.summary: Khiar is a fishing village of clay-mound people on the southern cape of Okuwun-Rahei, near the Seafalls coast. It supplies fish to the whole east.

notes.text: A cape village south of Seafalls, the confederacy's southern coastal outlier. No UESP page for Khiar.
Founded as a fishing station to feed the mound country, then a village; the Mazurath ruin on the next headland is older than anyone's memory.
A steady fishing village. Its boats go out at dawn and sell to Seafalls; its people dislike the Skeith smugglers' habit of landing at the cape.
About nine Argonians of the Oxhu-Teeleel; fishermen, net-makers and an old boat-wright.
Dried and salted fish, shell-fish, and boat-timber; they trade fish for clay goods and for Seafalls pearls.
The village sends eggs inland. Fishermen leave a clay fish at the cape for good catches.
Reed houses on stilts on a low rise above a sandy cape, nets and fish-racks on every pole, a stone breakwater of piled clay, salt wind.
Surf, crocodiles at the inlet, and Mazurath's ghosts on the headland.
The boat-wright is building a ship for a stranger who paid in old Velothi bronze. The headland ruin has started to glow after dark.

records.name: Redclay Watch
records.held_by: Aroxhu confederacy spear-watch
records.summary: Redclay Watch is a mound-top spear-post on the road between Renhu and Seafalls. The confederacy keeps it to take tolls on outside goods.

notes.text: A watchpost of the Oxhu-Teeleel on a mound above the Renhu-Seafalls road. The name is ours; no UESP page exists.
Built after Arorha's boatmen lost goods to coast robbers, and manned by volunteers from Renhu and Khiar.
A watch of five spears, with a bar across the road and a toll box. They pass Seafalls folk and Aroxhu carts free and charge outsiders.
Five Argonians on rotation from Renhu and Khiar, led by a woman of Khiar who knows the road.
Tolls and small fines. The confederacy's treasury sees a quarter.
None official; the spear-watch carry hatching-stones from home villages.
A clay mound with a palisade of cut reeds, a round thatched watch-hut, a bar across the road, a cluster of spears in a rack.
Smuggler bands, tribal raiders from the Sarpa camp, and the bad road in the monsoon.
The watch have caught a smuggler with Archwarden stamps on his bills; the leader wants someone neutral to carry him to Aroxhu.

records.name: Vicrium
records.held_by: Seafalls families and Aroxhu clay-miners, jointly
records.summary: Vicrium is an old ochre and alum mine in the clay country behind Seafalls. The Imperial name stuck and its galleries run deeper than the miners care to go.

notes.text: A mine on the road between Renhu and Seafalls whose Imperial-sounding name marks an East Empire Company working. UESP has no page for Vicrium.

sources.title: East Empire Company wharves and stores outlast the Company (argonia-4e201-state.md)

notes.text: The Company's ochre and alum mine of the last Third Era, shut when the province closed in 4E 6; Aroxhu's clay-diggers and Seafalls families reopened the upper galleries.
The upper galleries are worked in the dry season; the lower ones are sealed with clay plugs after a gas-pocket killed two men.
About six miners, Oxhu clay-diggers and Seafalls families, led by a gallery-boss who keeps the key.
Ochre for dye and alum for fixing it. Both go to Aroxhu's dyers; any surplus is sold to Archon.
The miners leave a pot of ochre at the mouth. Their dead are mourned in Aroxhu.
A hillside cut in rust and yellow bands with a plank-lined adit, a Company-era timber headframe, ore carts, yellow-stained pools.
Cave-ins, poisonous gas in the lower galleries and a nest of crocodiles in the flooded drift.
The sealed galleries hold the Company's last strongbox. The gallery-boss wants a diver to see whether the flooded drift still connects.

records.name: Seafalls
records.held_by: The Spray-Folk of Seafalls, under their pilot-elder
records.summary: Seafalls is a cliff-and-surf village on the coast north of Archon, where a river drops to the sea. Its people pilot ships, keep a portage round the falls and live apart from the Hist.

notes.text: A coastal village at the falls where a river reaches the Padomaic, the reason cargo changes boats here. Canon names Seafalls as Archon's neighbour to the north-north-east and the settlement register calls it a falls-and-portage settlement; UESP has no page of its own.
The Spray-Folk came here from the Archon shore, beyond any Hist tree. Under the East Empire Company they ran the portage for Company boats; since 4E 6 the portage is theirs alone.
A small, self-contained village. Their pilots take ships into Archon and off the Thorn road; the Archwardens charge them nothing because nobody else will do the job.
About fourteen Argonians of the Spray-Folk: pilots, portage-men and net-menders. The pilot-elder, an old woman who has taken a hundred ships through the surf, is the village's voice.

The portage, which charges cargo-carriers by weight; piloting; pearl-shell and sea-salt; and a trade in drift-wood and wreck-salvage. Seafalls is the transfer point on the north-east link between Thorn, Branchmont and Archon.

They hold that the sea keeps the memories the Hist let fall. They leave painted shells and knotted cords at the falls, keep death-dancers for burials, and nest on the shoals. Hatching and naming mean a long journey inland.
White falls dropping into a sea-pool, stilt houses and nest-platforms on the cliff and shoals, rope-bridges over the spray, salt-crusted decks, the lighthouse beyond the point, gulls and surf.
Surf and spray on wet rocks, rope-bridge falls, sea-drakes in the bay, and Skeith pirate boats in the dark.
The pilot-elder needs a successor and has chosen a hatchling who cannot swim. A ship has come in with a cargo that does not match its bills, and the Archwardens want it quietly seized.

terrain_needs.why: on the cliff above the falls

records.name: Seafalls Lighthouse
records.held_by: The Spray-Folk of Seafalls, a keeper family
records.summary: Seafalls Lighthouse is the beacon on the point east of the village. A keeper family lights it each night to guide ships past the shoals.

notes.text: A tall beacon house on the point south-east of the falls, guarding ships from the shoals. The tower and its keepers are ours; there is no UESP page.
Built by the East Empire Company for its Archon-Thorn run; kept alight by the Spray-Folk since the Company left.
Lit every night by the keeper, who burns fish-oil bought from Archon and sells directions to the lost.
Three Argonians, a keeper and his two hatchlings; one of them is a trained watcher with a long glass.
Light-fees from the pilots of Seafalls, a share of salvage from every wreck on the shoals.
The keeper keeps a clay lamp for the lost dead and lights it with the beacon.
A white-lime tower of stone on the point, a gallery with a great brass lamp, a keeper's hut and a boat-slip, surf below.
Wind on the gallery, slippery rocks and the shoals; pirates sometimes douse the light to wreck a ship.
Someone has doused the light twice and a ship was lost. The keeper's hatchling saw a boat from Skeith Isle on the first night.

records.name: Brineflat Farm
records.held_by: A Seafalls family
records.summary: Brineflat Farm is a salt-and-sedge farm on the flats behind Seafalls, kept by one Spray-Folk family.

notes.text: A farm on the salt flats inland of Seafalls. The name is ours; no UESP page.
Cleared by a Seafalls family who wanted ground to grow what the sea would not give them.
A working holding that sells salt and sedge to Seafalls.
Three Argonians, a mother and two grown children.
Sea-salt boiled in clay pans, sedge for roofing, and hardy marsh vegetables. The family sells to Seafalls.
They go to Seafalls for the death-dances and keep a painted shell at the door.
Flat grey salt-pans, stacked sedge, a single reed house on a mound, drying racks, a boiling shed with a stack.
Mudcrabs, fleshflies and the odd smuggler passing on the road.
The family's youngest has found a smuggler's cache in the pans and is afraid to tell anyone.

records.name: Saltmeadow Farm
records.held_by: A Seafalls family
records.summary: Saltmeadow Farm is a grazing and rice farm south of Brineflat, kept by a Spray-Folk household that herds guar.

notes.text: A guar farm on the meadow between Seafalls and the Khiar road. The name is ours; no UESP page.
Founded by a Seafalls family who had fallen out with the pilot-elder and wanted their own ground.
A small guar herd and a rice paddy, with a path to Seafalls.
Four Argonians, two adults and two hatchlings.
Guar-hide, milk and rice, sold at Seafalls. A little of the herd goes to Archon on the pilots' boats.
They keep a clay figure of a guar at the door and do not trouble the sea-spirits.
A green meadow with guar, a rice paddy, a reed house on a low mound, a clay fence, and salt wind.
Crocodiles in the paddy, marsh predators for the herd, and smuggler thieves.
A guar has been taken and a foot-print leads toward the Vicrium mine. The family has an old grudge with the pilot-elder.

records.name: Tidewatch Homestead
records.held_by: A lone Spray-Folk household
records.summary: Tidewatch Homestead is a lone house on the shore south of Brineflat. Its household watches the surf and mends nets for Seafalls.

notes.text: A solitary house above the shore between the farms and the sea. The name is ours; no UESP page.
Built by a net-mender who preferred quiet to the village.
A quiet house; the household sells nets and rope to Seafalls.
Two Argonians, an old net-mender and her niece.
Nets, rope, and cord of coast-grass, sold at Seafalls.
They hang votive cords on the fence, one for every wreck.
A single stilt house at the tide line, nets spread on the fence, a tarred boat on the shingle.
Surf, crabs and smugglers who sometimes land on the shingle at night.
The old net-mender once wove a net for a smuggler and knows his boat; she will tell a friend.

records.name: Icalca
records.held_by: The Agaceph of Icalca, a raft-folk
records.summary: Icalca is a hamlet of Agaceph raft-folk on the western lake. They read, cast illusions and freeze intruders before they decide what to do with them.

notes.text: An Agaceph hamlet on a lake in Okuwun-Rahei's west. No UESP page for Icalca; the Agaceph are canon in Middle Argonia.
The Agaceph looted the dead Maran monastery at Umpholo for its books in canon, and their hamlets hold such books; Icalca keeps a shelf of them.
A hamlet of raft-houses and stilts, bounded by reed screens. The Agaceph keep to their lake and sell books and illusions to those who ask politely.
About eight Agaceph with rainbow scales, needle-faced, riding razor-thin rafts; the eldest reads three languages.
Books, scrolls and illusion-work are sold or swapped. Fish and lake-grain keep the hamlet fed.
They hold a weak respect for the Hist, and read the Maran books for amusement.
Raft-houses lashed together on a blue-green lake, reed screens painted in bright scale-colours, long thin rafts hauled onto mats.
Illusions that freeze, confuse or misdirect strangers; lake crocodiles and the bandits Icalca keeps out.
The hamlet needs a book returned that a Gaweja fisher took. A Maran monastery tract in Icalca's shelf names a ruin no one has found.

records.name: Xibcan
records.held_by: The Agaceph of Xibcan
records.summary: Xibcan is an Agaceph hamlet on a marsh island. Its people keep a small library taken from a dead mission and charge outsiders to read it.

notes.text: A raft-and-stilt hamlet in the marsh between Gaweja and Renhu. No UESP page.
The hamlet grew round a mission library that its people took from a dead Maran outstation in the Third Era.
A hamlet that guards its shelf of books and charges for access.
About seven Agaceph, with a literate eldest who acts as librarian and keeps a ledger.
Reading fees, copied pages, illusion-work and eels. Prices are steep but fair.
They honour the Hist from a distance and read the missionary's tracts as comedy.
Raft-houses and stilts on a marsh pond, books drying on lines in the sun, rafts hauled onto reed beds.
Illusion traps and lost-looking reed paths; marsh crocodiles, leeches and fleshflies.
A page from the library has been cut out and sold; the librarian wants it back and will pay in books.

records.name: Yina
records.held_by: The Agaceph of Yina
records.summary: Yina is an Agaceph hamlet built round the foot of the Sethiral ruin. Its people live in the old stones, which they use as a library and a fort.

notes.text: A hamlet at the river bank where a Cantemiric Velothi ruin stands, on the map's own pairing of a hamlet and a ruin in one cell. No UESP page for Yina.
The Agaceph moved into the shell of a Velothi stronghold, and reuse its stone halls to store books; they are not afraid of ghosts.
A hamlet of stilt-houses leaning against the ruin's wall. They defend it against Skeith raiders and tribal bands alike.
About six Agaceph, with a scholar who has mapped the ruin's upper halls.
Books, illusion-work, and ash-glass shards; they trade a little with Renhu.
The Agaceph keep a respectful distance from the ruin's lower halls where the Velothi dead lie.
Raft-houses on the river, tied to the black Velothi wall, painted reed screens, books drying on the stone.
Ancestor ghosts in the lower halls, illusions on the approach and river crocodiles.
A sealed door in the ruin has begun to hum, and the scholar needs help opening it without waking the dead.

records.name: Yulca
records.held_by: The Agaceph of Yulca, a council of readers
records.summary: Yulca is the Agaceph's one town, on the great lake in Okuwun-Rahei's west. It is a town of readers, illusionists and rafters who keep books taken from dead missions.

notes.text: A raft-town on a wide lake in the west, the only Agaceph place of any size. No UESP page for Yulca; the Agaceph are canon in Middle Argonia, exclusive to it.
The Agaceph gathered here after the Maran missions died in the Third Era. They looted the Maran monastery at Umpholo for its library in canon, and Yulca keeps the most books of any place in the east.
A lake town of rafts, with a public reading-room. Agaceph here are polite and wary and will freeze an intruder with a spell before deciding what to do.
About twenty-two Agaceph in rainbow colours; the council of readers has five members. A few visitors from Gaweja and Aroxhu live in a guest raft.
Books, scrolls, ink, illusion-work and spell-teaching, sold for coin, fish and rice. Yulca's reading-room charges outsiders; its illusions are cheap.
No Hist grows here; they think the Hist loud and their books better company. They keep a hall of the Maran dead's tracts to read for sport.
A town of lashed rafts and stilted pavilions on a broad lake, reed screens in bright scale-colours, a reading-room under a tall roof, books drying on lines, rafts like blades on the water.
Illusion and paralysis spells on strangers; otherwise the town is calm. The lake has crocodiles and a pirate-raft rumour.
The reading-room's most prized book has been stolen. A scholar wants a Maran tract translated, and no one in Yulca will say why.

records.name: Tazhul
records.held_by: Root-Folk of Helstrom, an egg-tending station
records.summary: Tazhul is a small Root-Folk station in the marsh west of Inoja, a hunting and egg-tending post of Helstrom's people far from their Hist.

notes.text: An unlabelled forest-green triangle on the map: a Root-Folk station on the edge of Okuwun-Rahei. The name is ours, in Argonian style; no UESP page.
The Root-Folk keep stations through the inner swamp; Tazhul was set up to tend eggs on a warm mud-bank and hunt the marsh.
A small station with a rack of eggs and a hunters' lodge; the Root-Folk keep apart from the mounds and the Agaceph.
About four Saxhleel, hunters and an egg-minder; wary of strangers.
Hunting, eggs, and sap-gathering; they sell hides and skins to Aroxhu.
The eggs are warmed to a rhythm they say the Hist sets from afar; they hold no tree here.
Root-hollow lodges and stilt-houses on a mud-bank, egg-racks, drying hides, marsh herons.
Crocodiles, giant snakes and the Root-Folk's own traps on every path.
Two eggs have failed to hatch and the egg-minder believes someone has cursed them. A hunter has found a Sarpa feather in a trap.

records.name: Seth-Alaxh Roost
records.held_by: The Sarpa of the Seth-Alaxh roost
records.summary: Seth-Alaxh Roost is a winged Sarpa camp in the marsh between Aroxhu and Yulca. They are hostile to strangers and drive them off by air.

notes.text: A permanent Sarpa camp on a high mud-bank west of Aroxhu. The name is ours; no UESP page.
The Sarpa are canon as winged and hostile to outsiders, exclusive to Middle Argonia; a camp on the edge of Oxhu country is consistent with the confederacy's frequent skirmishes with them.
A camp of perches and tents; Aroxhu's spears and the Sarpa fight now and then and make peace without grudge.
About eight Sarpa led by a wing-chief with a scarred crest.
Feathers, eggs and raided goods; they trade fish for clay beads.
They read omens in the wind and speak of the Hist as the sky's roots.
Tall perches and streamers over a mud-bank, tents of reed and hide, rope nets, droppings white on stones.
Air-borne archers and sudden raids; they attack at dusk.
The wing-chief wants a stolen perch-pole returned from Aroxhu. An Aroxhu spear-captain wants peace and needs an envoy.

records.name: Anvadas
records.held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts
records.summary: Anvadas is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding on a mud-ridge in the marsh south of Gaweja.

notes.text: Anvadas is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding on a mud-ridge in the marsh south of Gaweja. It is unnamed on the map; the name is ours, in Velothi style. UESP has no page for it, and the Velothi are canon for this coast.
Cantemiric Velothi settled the eastern seaboard; the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 ended them, and Anvadas was empty within a generation.
A ruin half-swallowed by marsh, avoided by the Oxhu and Agaceph alike.
No one lives at Anvadas, and the Oxhu and Agaceph keep clear of the mud-ridge. The household's ghosts stay in the flooded courtyard and the tower.
Once a river-fort. Now a scavenger's draw for Velothi bronze, ash-glass and carved tablets.

The Cantemiric household kept altar niches in each room and carved family tablets, and served a Daedric power in the lower hall. The marsh has drowned the hall, but the tablets are still said to answer the right voice.
Dark Velothi stonework in heavy courses, tilted and sunk, reeds in the courtyard, a leaning tower, still black pools within.
Ancestor ghosts, skeletal guards, crocodiles in the flooded halls.
A sealed vault door has a lock that opens to the family tablet. A scholar from Yulca wants any Velothi book that survives.

terrain_needs.why: the ruin stands on a ridge
the halls are cut into the ridge

records.name: Sethiral
records.held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts
records.summary: Sethiral is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding at Yina, on the river bank above the hamlet.

notes.text: Sethiral is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding at Yina, on the river bank above the hamlet. It is unnamed on the map; the name is ours, in Velothi style. UESP has no page for it, and the Velothi are canon for this coast.
The Cantemiric Velothi built it and the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 killed them; the Agaceph moved in at its foot soon after.
The upper halls are used by Yina's Agaceph as a reading place; the lower halls are shut.
No one lives in Sethiral's halls; Yina's Agaceph read in the upper rooms and leave at dusk. The household's ghosts keep to the lower halls, behind the humming door.
Once a river-fort. The Agaceph trade ash-glass shards from its upper halls.

The household's ancestor tablets and altar niches survive in the upper halls, where Yina's readers copy them with respect. The lower hall's Daedric shrine is shut, and the Agaceph say it is better left so.
A black stone keep with a broken tower on a river bank, ivy, vines, reed rafts moored under the wall.
Ancestor ghosts in the lower halls, a humming sealed door and the river crocodiles.
The sealed door hums at night. Yina's scholar will pay for anyone who can read the Velothi script above it.

records.summary: Mazurath is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding on the headland south of Khiar.

notes.text: Mazurath is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding on the headland south of Khiar. It is unnamed on the map; the name is ours, in Velothi style. UESP has no page for it, and the Velothi are canon for this coast.
A Velothi coastal hold, ended by the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560. The headland has been unoccupied since.
A ruin on a sea-cliff, glowing faintly after dark, which the village of Khiar blames on its ghosts.
No one lives on Mazurath's headland, and Khiar's villagers will not go up after dark. The household's ghosts are blamed for the glow on the sea-cliff.
Once a coastal watch-hold. Now a draw for scavengers and the occasional smuggler's cache.
The coastal hold kept the Velothi ancestor rites, with a niche and tablet for each family dead. The shrine in the lower hall served a Daedric power, and its spell-fire on the upper tier still burns.
Black stone on a cliff edge, a broken sea-tower, salt crust, sea-birds nesting in the roof, surf below.
Ghosts, collapsing floors, and a sea-cave where the tide runs in.
A lamp-lit beacon on the upper tier still burns with a spell-fire; a captive Khiar fisherman was seen on it. A smuggler's cache lies in the sea-cave.

terrain_needs.why: the ruin stands on the headland
